title: Al-Muhyi, the Giver of Life
tomorrow: if life is His, what do Muslims say when someone dies?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Mu'id: He brings back, and the door stays open for anyone turning back. The line: he brings back. A new week opens on a prophet who wants to see it happen.
screen: `HE BRINGS BACK.` → `A PROPHET WANTS TO SEE IT.`

segments.voice: A seed in a paper cup on a classroom windowsill. You water it, and nothing. Water it, nothing. Then one morning there's a green hook pushing up through the dirt, and the whole class crowds around. Abraham wants to see something like that, only far bigger. In Surah al-Baqarah he says, in Pickthall's words: "My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead." And God answers with a question of His own: "Dost thou not believe?"
screen: `A SEED IN A PAPER CUP.` → `SHOW ME HOW.` → `DOST THOU NOT BELIEVE?`

segments.voice: Abraham's answer is a very human line: "Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease." He believes. He just wants his heart to catch up with what he believes. And he isn't scolded. He's given something to do. Take four birds, the verse says, and tame them to yourself. Then set a part of them on each hill, and call them, and they will come to you in haste. Some readers notice the taming: Abraham has to know these birds first, so that when they come flying back, he'll know they're the same ones. Today's Name is Al-Muhyi, the Giver of Life. And the Qur'an keeps a smaller picture of it in plain view. In Surah ar-Rum: "Look, therefore, at the prints of Allah's mercy (in creation): how He quickeneth the earth after her death." To quicken is old English for to make alive, not to speed up. Dry, cracked ground, then rain, then green. Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: in the Qur'an, a prophet asks for proof so his heart can rest, and the answer is a hands-on lesson with birds he had to get to know first.
screen: `SO MY HEART MAY BE AT EASE.` · `FOUR BIRDS, TAMED, THEN CALLED.` · `HE QUICKENETH THE EARTH.` · `QUICKEN MEANS MAKE ALIVE.` · then, large: `LIFE IS HIS.`

segments.voice: If there's a plant near you, touch the soil to see if it's dry, and water it slowly if it is. If there's a pet, sit with it. If neither, look out a window at one living thing, a tree, a bird, grass pushing through pavement, and keep it company for the two minutes.
screen: `ONE LIVING THING.` · `WATER IT, OR KEEP IT COMPANY.`

segments.voice: Al-Muhyi. The Giver of Life: to dead ground after rain, to four birds on four hills, and to the dead.
A line for the road: life is his, in the seedling on the sill and in the one listening. Fifteen thirty-four, done.

howItsDone: Muslims call on Allah as Al-Muhyi, the Giver of Life, and the Qur'an's verses of rain reviving dead earth are recited as signs of His power to give life again.

fork.setup: your friend believes, but before a big surgery he says, 'i want to SEE that it'll be ok.' someone tells him that's weak faith. what does Abraham's story say?
options: they're right; real faith never asks for anything.
asking so the heart can be at ease is in the Qur'an, from Abraham.
he should stop believing until he gets his proof.
fork.reveal: Abraham believed and still asked, 'that my heart may be at ease.' he wasn't scolded; he was given the birds.

original.note: Arabic: the Giver of Life. in Surah ar-Rum, Pickthall calls Him the Quickener of the Dead.

trapdoor: what you thought: God switches life on at birth, once.
what it means: life is given by Him again and again: to dead ground after rain, and to the dead.
what a scholar hears: 2:260 (Abraham's birds) beside 30:50 ('quickeneth the earth after her death'), the revived earth read as a sign of resurrection.
guess: the Giver of Life, to earth and to the dead
the Healer who cures every illness
the Creator who made the first life only

chat.says: dadi's tomato plants out back are half dead. nobody watered while she was in the hospital. pull them?
options: Water them and give it a week. The Qur'an pictures dead ground coming back.
Pull them. Dead is dead; buy new ones before she sees.
Leave them. If Allah wants them alive, they'll live without you.
chat.meaning: Al-Muhyi gives life, and the Qur'an shows dead earth quickened after rain. Caring for a living thing is how we take part.
